newsitem.title: GERMANY: German jobless could be halved-Labour Office Chief.
newsitem.headline: German jobless could be halved-Labour Office Chief.

text.p: The number of jobless in Germany could be halved by the year 2002 if the country's labour market becomes more flexible, the President of the German Labour Office said on German radio on Sunday.
Bernhard Jagoda said that certain conditions aimed at introducing more flexibity into Germany's rigid employment structures need to be met if jobless numbers are to be cut.
In June there were 4.37 million out of work in Germany and unemployment for the year is expected to average at a post-war record of 4.3 million.

Overtime needs to be cut by 40 percent, Jagoda said. The percentage of part-time workers has to rise, supplementary wage costs need to be cut by two percent and wages should only rise in line with inflation, he said.
On Friday the German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said that he was sticking to his target of halving the number of jobless by the year 2000.
